CHIEF COMPLAINT
Breast reduction consultation

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
25-year-old female presenting for consultation regarding breast reduction. She has been considering this procedure for 6-7 years. She reports back and upper back/neck pain beginning in high school, worsening with prolonged desk work. She has attended chiropractor appointments for a few years for management of her back pain. She experiences bra strap indentations on her shoulders. She wears a 34E sports bra, which she finds more comfortable and more affordable than regular bras in her size. She reports her breasts are constantly sweaty but denies rashes. She sometimes experiences numbness or tingling in her hands and occasionally has nipple pain. She reports activity limitation - she must hold her breasts when exercising, jumping, or running, which causes pain. She has no children currently but may plan to have children in the future. She has never consulted anyone previously about breast reduction. She has not had mammography; screening is recommended to begin at age 30 given her family history of breast cancer.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Back and neck/upper back pain since high school. Bra strap indentations. Occasional numbness/tingling in hands. Occasional nipple pain. Constantly sweaty breasts. No rashes underneath breasts. Activity limitation with pain during exercise.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Ongoing chiropractic care for back pain for a few years. Otherwise healthy.

MEDICATIONS
Propranolol

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother diagnosed with breast cancer at age 40.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Currently studying psychology. Drinks wine occasionally. Denies tobacco and drug use. Recently lost 10 pounds with goal of losing 20 more pounds. Husband recently accepted new job; patient transitioning to his insurance plan in July.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Breasts: Asymmetrical with severe ptosis bilaterally. No nipple retraction or discharge. No breast tenderness, masses, or axillary lymphadenopathy. One breast lower than the other.

RESULTS
Current bra size 34E (approximately G cup). Body surface area 2.65 m². Minimum required resection by Schnur scale: 1,792 grams. Anticipated post-reduction breast size: small C cup. Potential for nipple graft.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
25-year-old female with symptomatic macromastia for evaluation of bilateral reduction mammoplasty. Appropriate candidate for surgery. Has attempted nonsurgical treatment with minimal relief. Surgical plan: Bilateral reduction mammoplasty with removal of excess tissue and fat, breast lifting, and nipple repositioning. Incision pattern includes circumareolar, vertical, and inframammary components forming an anchor pattern. Expected surgery duration: 3 hours. Bilateral drains to be placed and remain for approximately 1 week. Clear plastic tape to be placed over incisions. Overnight hospital stay planned. Anticipated post-operative course includes bruising that will resolve over time. Scars expected to mature over approximately 1 year and may appear red initially. Nipple sensation typically preserved but small risk of alteration. Counseled that approximately 30% of patients are unable to breastfeed post-operatively. Discussed that breasts may enlarge with weight gain or pregnancy. Post-operative activity restrictions: No heavy lifting and no driving for 2-3 weeks, with total activity restrictions for approximately 6 weeks. Plan: Photos will be obtained today. Symptom documentation will be submitted to insurance company for authorization determination. Patient currently has Blue Cross Blue Shield insurance and will transition to husband's insurance plan in July. Insurance authorization submission will be completed once new insurance provider information is obtained. Upon insurance approval, office will coordinate surgery date. Pre-operative visit will be scheduled prior to surgery to address additional questions and review detailed post-operative instructions.
